messages:
Alex Kim: hey all, new hire here — first PR's CI failed on Buildkite. Not sure if it's my setup or perms. build shows a 403 when trying to fetch the repo. Anyone know who to ping for CI permissions?
Buildkite Bot: Build #412 (alex/feature/onboarding-ci) failed · exit code 1 · check logs: https://buildkite.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/builds/412
Alex Kim: here's the checkout error from the agent: 
```
remote: HTTP Basic: Access denied
fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference.git/'
```
Priya Patel: welcome! :tada: 2 quick things — make sure you added your SSH key to GitHub and that you're in the eng-infra or eng-ci team. also Buildkite needs you added to the pipeline/team. pinging infra folks.
Alex Kim: I added my ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub to GitHub but still getting the same thing. I think Buildkite is using HTTPS checkout here?
Samir Rao: hey @Alex Kim — welcome! likely Buildkite is configured to use the repo's HTTPS checkout and relies on a deploy key or org-level machine user. I can check. Can you paste the pipeline name?
Alex Kim: pipeline is "redwood-inference/build-and-test" (the PR triggered it).
Samir Rao: ok. quick workaround: if you go to your GitHub profile -> Settings -> SSH and GPG keys and confirm the key shows, run `ssh -T git@github.com` from the build node to confirm (locally just to sanity-check). But real fix: I need to add you to the GitHub team that the pipeline uses, and add you to the Buildkite pipeline team. I'll do that now.
Infra Oncall: also FYI we've had a couple of first-weekers run into this because the pipeline switched from SSH to HTTPS recently for dockerized agents. If someone is stuck, we usually add their user to the "eng-ci" GitHub team which gives the token access.
Alex Kim: thanks — I'm not in any org teams yet.
Samir Rao: done — added you to github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/teams/eng-ci and gave Buildkite access to your account on the pipeline. you should be able to re-run the build. I also bumped the pipeline to use the org deploy token for checkout.
Alex Kim: re-ran the build — now hitting a test flake that looks like a cache issue: 
```
Error: module import failed: corrupted cached wheel
Traceback: ...
```
Priya Patel: ah yeah we hit that with the docker layer cache last week. Try re-running with cache cleared or set env var SKIP_CACHE=1 in the buildkite "Manual" run. There's a small checkbox in the UI to clear caches.
Marta Nguyen: onboarding doc with steps here: https://redwood.internal/docs/onboarding/ci — includes checklist: add SSH key, join eng-ci team, verify Buildkite pipeline membership, how to re-run with clear cache.
Samir Rao: I cleared the cache for the build and kicked it. Also added a small CI guard so that failing cached installs get retried automatically.
Buildkite Bot: Build #413 (alex/feature/onboarding-ci) passed · duration 9m · https://buildkite.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/builds/413
Alex Kim: awesome, green! thanks @Samir, @Priya, @Marta. Saved my first-week nerves :relieved:
Priya Patel: welcome aboard and congrats on the green build :party_parrot:
Alex Kim: quick Q — for GitHub Actions workflows in other repos, do I need any extra perms? I'm planning a small infra tweak in a different repo.
Samir Rao: for Actions you usually need repo write access to commit workflow changes. For protected branches we may require an approver. If it's just editing workflow files, ask eng-sec if the repo has restricted actions. If you hit blocked runs, ping me or @Infra Oncall and we'll check the repo settings.
Alex Kim: got it, thanks. I'll follow the onboarding checklist and reach out if anything else pops up.
Marta Nguyen: tagging this thread in the onboarding tracker so we can mark "CI access" as done.
Alex Kim: thanks everyone!
